title: App-based cognitive Training in elderly Patients: Feasability and acceptance in geriatric and gerontopsychiatric populations
summary: The aim of the study is to investigate whether and to what extent older patients in geriatric and geriatric psychiatry can use a smartphone app to train their cognitive abilities during a hospital stay and subsequently in their daily lives at home. Medical treatment is provided exclusively as part of routine care. Participation in the study does not entail any additional therapeutic measures. Data on app usage will be collected, particularly regarding frequency, duration, and regularity of use, as well as any premature discontinuation of use. In addition, medical data, mobility data collected via wearable sensors, and information from questionnaires and interviews will be gathered. Among other things, the study will examine digital literacy, attitudes toward digital applications, quality of life, and experiences with the app. The study focuses on whether the app can be integrated into daily life in both inpatient and home settings and is acceptable to patients. Additionally, differences between geriatric and gerontopsychiatric patients regarding app usage, other clinical characteristics, and mobility will be examined.
conditions: The Use of Digital Cognitive Training Applications in Geriatrics and Geriatric Psychiatry

interventions.name: Within the first two days of admission, a geriatric baseline assessment is conducted, including evaluations of cognition, mobility, depressive symptoms and daily living functionality, as well as digital literacy and technology acceptance, self-efficacy, and participation. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients are eligible for inclusion if they own a smartphone and meet at least one of the following criteria: they are aged ≥65 years, they are aged 50–64 years and have at least two chronic conditions, or they are aged ≥60 years and have a diagnosed mental disorder. Sufficient mobility is also required for study participation, defined as the ability to stand unsupported for at least 10 seconds and to walk at least three meters with or without a walking aid. Both cognitively unimpaired and cognitively impaired patients may be included, provided that, based on clinical judgment, they have sufficient comprehension and language proficiency to participate in the study (sufficient German language proficiency and hearing ability). In addition, an inpatient stay of at least 14 days must be anticipated.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients are excluded if, based on neuropsychological testing or clinical judgment, they have a severe psychiatric disorder (e.g., acute psychosis, severe depression with suicidality, or a manic episode) or severe dementia (MoCA ≤ 5). Patients are also excluded if sensory or motor impairments, such as severe visual impairment, coordination disorders, or paresis, prevent them from using the app. Further exclusion criteria include medical contraindications to mobility (e.g., permanent immobility, untreated fractures, active bleeding, or shock) and contraindications to app use, such as epilepsy or other conditions associated with seizures or impaired consciousness. Patients receiving palliative care and those concurrently participating in studies investigating cognitive training or mobility as an outcome are also excluded.
